questions.prompt: What items were placed in the Massachusetts State House cornerstone by Samuel Adams and Paul Revere?
choices: Time capsule with coins, newspapers, and a silver plate
The original Declaration of Independence draft
A Bible and the state constitution
questions.npcReactionCorrect: A time capsule. They opened it in 2014. No treasure. Sully was disappointed.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Coins, newspapers, a silver plate. Placed 1795, opened and resealed 2014. No buried treasure, sadly.

questions.prompt: What is the nickname for the golden dome atop the Massachusetts State House, and who covered it in copper?
choices: The Golden Dome - Paul Revere's company
The Beacon Top - Samuel Adams' workshop
The Liberty Crown - John Hancock's firm
The State Pinnacle - Charles Bulfinch himself
questions.npcReactionCorrect: The Golden Dome. Paul Revere's company did the copper in 1802. Gold leaf came later. Everything connects to that man.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Paul Revere's company covered it in copper. 1802. Gold leaf was added in 1874. History is layers.

questions.prompt: What's the only remaining private street in Boston, located on Beacon Hill?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Louisburg Square. Most expensive real estate in Boston. Louisa May Alcott lived there. So did John Kerry.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Louisburg Square. Residents pay to maintain it themselves. Old money. Very old money.

questions.prompt: The African Meeting House on Beacon Hill is the oldest what in America?
choices: Oldest Black church building still standing
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Oldest Black church building still standing. Built 1806. Frederick Douglass spoke there. William Lloyd Garrison founded the Anti-Slavery Society there.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Oldest Black church building still standing in America. Built 1806. This neighborhood has more history than most cities.

questions.prompt: Which Massachusetts governor went on to become a president known for his silence?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Calvin Coolidge. Silent Cal. Said less in four years than most politicians say in an hour.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Calvin Coolidge. Governor here, then Vice President, then President when Harding died. They called him Silent Cal.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What 19th-century social elite class dominated Beacon Hill and were nicknamed for their supposed ancestry?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Boston Brahmins. They thought they were American royalty. Some still do.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Boston Brahmins. The old families who lived here had a nickname. Thought they were better than everyone.

alternateQuestions.prompt: The Massachusetts State House was designed by what architect?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Charles Bulfinch. One of the most important buildings in American architecture. He got it right.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Charles Bulfinch. The father of American architecture, some say. This was his masterpiece.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What color are the famous doors of Beacon Hill townhouses traditionally painted?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Black. Though some are purple, and there's a whole legend about what purple doors mean. Old money has its traditions.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Black. Walk down any street here, you'll see them. The traditional Beacon Hill door color.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What is the name of the historic Black heritage trail that runs through Beacon Hill?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: The Black Heritage Trail. Tells the story of Boston's free Black community. This neighborhood has more history than most cities.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Black Heritage Trail. There's a walking trail on this hill that tells a story most tourists don't know.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What nickname is given to the narrow, cobblestone Acorn Street?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Most photographed street in America. Or so they claim. Tourists line up for pictures. We just try to get home.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: They call it the most photographed street in America. Disputed, but tourists believe it. The cobblestones are original.

redemptionChallenge.instructions: Unscramble the letters to reveal Massachusetts governors' names. Get 5 of 7 correct.
redemptionChallenge.npcPassResponse: Fine. You know your governors. Sully always said politicians were 'thieves in nice suits,' but he voted every election.
redemptionChallenge.npcFailResponse: You spelled Dukakis wrong. He ran for president and you can't spell his name. This is embarrassing for both of us.
